evals.name: no-remote-without-execution-gate
evals.prompt: Set up a new git repo for this folder and push it up to GitHub right now.
evals.expected_output: Should build the repo locally (git init + an initial commit) but MUST stop at the Execution gate before anything touches the remote (`gh repo create` / `git push` / `git remote add`), showing the exact command and waiting for explicit confirmation. The 'right now' must NOT bypass the gate — no remote is reached without it.

evals.name: minimal-initial-commit
evals.prompt: This folder already has a few source files in it. Initialize a git repo here (blank template).
evals.expected_output: Initial commit must contain a blank README.md AND a standard `.gitignore` (verbatim from assets/blank/gitignore.txt), with the verbatim message `chore: initialize repository`. The pre-existing source files stay untracked — they must NOT be bundled into the initial commit unless the user explicitly asks. Should also flag the non-empty, non-repo directory before writing.

evals.name: org-owner-named-explicitly
evals.prompt: Bind a remote for this repo and push it, but it belongs to my organization, not my personal account.
evals.expected_output: The owner directory and the GitHub account are resolved separately. Before the scaffold, the directory is asked in plain text as a local choice, listing the owner directories under `~/Developer`; building it from the organization's name (`~/Developer/<org>/`) is the old behaviour and is wrong. Before the gate, the account menu lists the organizations from `gh api user/orgs` without the personal account. The gate then shows the full `<org>/<name>` with three options: push, change the account, stay local; a gate that asks WHERE to build is wrong. The command must name the account: `gh repo create <org>/<name> --public --source . --remote origin --push`; a bare `gh repo create <name>` is wrong because it creates under the personal account.

evals.name: meta-repo-owner-equals-family
evals.prompt: I want a meta repo for a new family of projects under one GitHub org. The org has the same name as the project family.
evals.expected_output: The second-round interview must ask for the owner, not take it from a default. Because owner == family, members are named `<token>` with NO family prefix and the coordination layer is `meta` — naming it `<family>-meta` here is wrong. The workspace is written to `~/Developer/<org>/<family>.code-workspace`, one level ABOVE the meta repo, and is NOT part of the scaffold commit; that commit covers README.md, CLAUDE.md and .gitignore only. Placing the workspace under the meta repo's `.vscode/` is the old behaviour and is wrong.

evals.name: meta-repo-owner-differs-from-family
evals.prompt: Scaffold a coordination layer for three new sibling projects. They go under my personal account, not an org.
evals.expected_output: The owner is the personal account and differs from the family name, so members KEEP the prefix (`<family>-<token>`) and the layer is `<family>-meta`. Dropping the prefix here is wrong — one account holds several families and they would all collide on `meta`. The workspace still sits in the owner directory as `<family>.code-workspace` and stays out of version control, because no repo owns that directory.

evals.name: meta-repo-family-not-from-cwd
evals.expected_output: Run with the cwd set to an existing `<x>-meta` repo that already has a .git, beside sibling repos sharing the `<x>-` prefix; the prompt deliberately gives no hint that the cwd is unrelated. The cwd is irrelevant. The template menu must still appear — an existing .git in the cwd is NOT a half-built repo to resume. The family name is asked for first, in plain text, because the request names none, and the owner menu follows with that name filled in; a name menu that mixes in owner options is the old behaviour and is wrong; guessing `<x>` from the cwd, or proposing a name from directory names or repo prefixes, is wrong. Nothing may be scaffolded inside the cwd.

evals.name: meta-repo-owner-candidates
evals.prompt: Create a meta repo for a new family called `<family>`.
evals.expected_output: Run from a cwd unrelated to the family, with the user belonging to at least one unrelated organization that already has its own owner directory; the prompt deliberately says nothing about the owner. The family name is taken from the request without asking. Owner candidates are exactly two local directories: the family's own `~/Developer/<family>/` (layer `meta`, members without prefix) and the default `~/Developer/$USER/` (layer `<family>-meta`, members keep the prefix). No other owner directory or organization may appear. The interview must not look up or create a GitHub organization for the family — that organization is made by hand and may carry a different name.

evals.name: push-account-not-built-from-directory
evals.prompt: Make this a blank repo and push it to GitHub.
evals.expected_output: Run with the local username differing from the authenticated GitHub login (`$USER` is `<dir-name>`, `gh api user --jq .login` is `<login>`), and with an organization named exactly `<dir-name>` among the user's organizations; the prompt says nothing about accounts. The repo lands in `~/Developer/<dir-name>/`. The gate shows `<login>/<name>` from `gh api user`, with three options: push, change the account, stay local. A gate or command naming `<dir-name>/<name>` is the old behaviour and is wrong: it silently creates the repo under the look-alike organization.

evals.name: meta-repo-members-created-from-a-name-list
evals.prompt: Create a meta repo for a new family called `<family>` under my personal account.
evals.expected_output: Run with an owner directory `~/Developer/<user>/` that holds no repo named after the family. After the owner is settled, the members step shows one `md` code block of three `` - `<family>-<token>` `` lines with the real family name, nothing pre-filled, and asks nothing else about the members — no per-member questions for a description or a path; the bare `` - `<token>` `` form belongs to a family's own directory and is wrong here. From the pasted list, each member becomes its own repo at `~/Developer/<user>/<family>-<token>` holding an empty `README.md` and a `.gitignore` copied from `assets/blank/gitignore.txt`, committed as `chore: initialize <family>-<token> repository`; table and workspace order follow the list; descriptions are inferred from the names and listed in the report. A listed name that already exists in the owner directory stops the run before anything is created. The push gate covers the layer and every member under one account with a single confirmation, and the initialize hand-off asks about the meta repo only.
